intro: Some things are real, but you cannot see them. You feel the wind. You know when someone loves you. The Bible tells about an unseen world too. It tells of God's home, called heaven.
In this unit, you will meet the Bible's heavenly helpers. It calls them angels and sons of God. You will meet Michael Heiser. He was a teacher who read the Bible's old languages.
Then you will visit a garden called Eden. You will hear about a trick, a choice and a kind gift. You will be able to retell these stories. You will say what Heiser thought about them.
bigQuestion: What do the Bible's first stories tell about God's home and God's family?

timeline.t: The wind lifts a kite. It is real, but you cannot see it.
The Bible tells of heaven as God's home.
Jacob dreams of angels going up and down a ladder (Genesis 28).
The sons of God shout for joy when the world is made (Job 38:7).
God makes light, sky, land, plants, animals and people (Genesis 1).
God plants a garden in Eden. People care for it (Genesis 2).
A serpent tricks Eve. People choose not to listen (Genesis 3).
God makes clothes for Adam and Eve before they leave (Genesis 3:21).
Angels bring shepherds good news of great joy (Luke 2).

words.d: not able to be seen with your eyes
the place the Bible calls God's home
a heavenly helper in the Bible who does what God asks
a Bible name for heavenly ones who live near God
someone who brings news from one person to another
the garden home in the Bible's first story
an old word for a snake; in Genesis 3, the one who tricked Eve
picking one thing to do instead of another

test.q: Which of these is real but unseen?
test.why: You cannot see the wind. But you can feel it and see what it does.

test.q: What does the Bible call God's home?
test.why: The Bible tells of heaven as God's home.

test.q: What did Jacob see in his dream in Genesis 28?
test.why: Genesis 28 says Jacob dreamed of angels going up and down a ladder.

test.q: In Job 38:7, what did the sons of God do when the world was made?
test.why: Job 38:7 says the sons of God shouted for joy.

choices: A teacher who read the Bible's old languages
test.why: Heiser was a teacher who read the Bible's old languages, like Hebrew and Greek.

test.q: What did Heiser call the heavenly ones?
test.why: Heiser thought the heavenly ones were like God's family in heaven.

test.q: What does the Hebrew word for angel mean?
test.why: The Hebrew word for angel means messenger. Angels bring news.

test.q: Where did God put the first man to work and care?
test.why: Genesis 2 says God put the man in the garden of Eden to work it and keep it.

choices: As God's home on earth where two families met
test.why: Heiser saw Eden as God's home on earth, where his heavenly and earthly families met.

test.q: What kind thing did God do in Genesis 3:21?
choices: Made clothes for Adam and Eve
test.why: Genesis 3:21 says God made clothes for Adam and Eve. It shows he still cared.

write.prompt: Tell or draw: Who does the Bible say lives in the unseen world? Use two stories from this unit, like Job 38:7 and Genesis 28. Say what the story says. Then say what Michael Heiser thought.
tips: Name the book, like Job or Genesis.
Say what the story says first.
Use a word from this unit, like angel or heaven.

title: God's Family in Heaven

chapters.title: Who Lives in the Unseen World?
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the Bible say about a world we cannot see?

story.title: The Kite and the Wind
story.kicker: Rosa's kite flies high. But she cannot see what holds it up.
paragraphs: It is a windy day at the park. Rosa holds the string of her red kite. The kite jumps up. It climbs high over the trees. The string pulls hard in her hand.
Rosa looks up. She squints. "Grandpa, what is holding my kite up?" Grandpa smiles. "The wind is," he says. Rosa looks all around. "But I can't see the wind!"
"No," says Grandpa. "But you can feel it on your face. You can see it move the leaves. Some things are real, but we can't see them. Love is like that too."
Grandpa sits on the bench. "The Bible tells about an unseen world too," he says. "It tells of God's home and of heavenly helpers. Want to hear about them?" Rosa nods and sits down beside him.
story.think: Name something you cannot see but you know is there. How do you know?

lessons.title: You Cannot See the Wind
lessons.mainIdea: Some things are real even when we cannot see them.
reading: Look out the window. The trees bend. A flag flaps. You cannot see the wind. But you can see what it does. You can feel it on your cheeks.
Something *unseen* is something you cannot see with your eyes. The wind is unseen. The air you breathe is unseen. But they are still there.
Love is unseen too. You cannot hold love in your hand. But you see a hug. You hear a kind word. That is how you know love is there.

words.d: not able to be seen with your eyes

look.title: The Moving Leaves
look.text: Look at the big tree in the yard. Its leaves wiggle and shake. A paper bag rolls across the grass. Nobody is pushing it. Your hair blows into your eyes.
look.prompt: What is moving the leaves and the bag? How can you tell?

check.q: Why do we know the wind is there?
choices: We can see what it does
We can hold it in a box
check.why: We cannot see the wind. But we see leaves move and feel it on our face.

check.q: What does unseen mean?
choices: Not able to be seen with your eyes
check.why: Unseen means you cannot see it with your eyes, like the wind or the air.

check.q: How can you tell love is there?
choices: You can hold it in your hand
You see a hug and hear kind words
check.why: Love is unseen. We know it by what people do, like a hug or a kind word.

lessons.title: God's Home in Heaven
lessons.mainIdea: The Bible tells of heaven as God's home.
reading: The Bible is a very old book. It tells about an unseen world. It says God has a home there. The Bible calls it *heaven*.
Jesus taught his friends a prayer. It starts by talking to God as a Father in heaven. You can read it in Matthew, chapter 6.
Many people believe heaven is real. Other people are not sure. In this course, you learn what the Bible says. You learn how people have read it.

words.d: the place the Bible calls God's home

look.title: A Prayer to God in Heaven
look.text: Jesus told his friends how to pray. He said to start like this: Our Father, who is in heaven, your name is holy.
look.cite: Matthew 6:9, retold in simple words from the World English Bible
look.prompt: Where does this prayer say God is?

check.q: What does the Bible call God's home?
check.why: The Bible calls God's home heaven.

check.q: Where can you read the prayer Jesus taught?
check.why: The prayer that starts with our Father in heaven is in Matthew, chapter 6.

check.q: What do you learn in this course?
choices: What the Bible says and how people read it
check.why: This course shows what the Bible says. It shows how people have read it. You think it through yourself.

lessons.title: Angels Going Up and Down
lessons.mainIdea: The Bible tells of heavenly helpers called angels.
reading: A man named Jacob went on a long trip. One night he slept outside. He put his head on a stone. Then he had a dream.
In the dream, Jacob saw a tall ladder. It went up to heaven. Angels went up and down on it. You can read this in Genesis, chapter 28.
The Bible tells of many angels. They are heavenly helpers. They do what God asks. In the Bible stories, they help people.

words.d: a heavenly helper in the Bible who does what God asks

look.title: Jacob's Dream
look.text: Picture a quiet night. The stars are out. Jacob sleeps on the ground. In his dream, a ladder reaches up to the sky. Bright helpers walk up and down it, calm and slow.
look.prompt: What did Jacob see going up and down the ladder?

check.q: What did Jacob see in his dream?
choices: A ladder with angels on it
check.why: Genesis 28 says Jacob dreamed of a ladder. Angels went up and down on it.

check.q: What is an angel in the Bible?
check.why: The Bible tells of angels as heavenly helpers who do what God asks.

check.q: Where can you read about Jacob's dream?
check.why: Jacob's dream of the ladder is in Genesis, chapter 28.

lessons.title: The Sons of God
lessons.mainIdea: The Bible also calls heavenly ones the sons of God.
reading: The Bible has more than one name for heavenly helpers. One name is angels. Another name is *sons of God*.
The book of Job uses this name. One day, it says, the sons of God came before God. You can read it in Job, chapter 1.
A son is part of a family. So the name sons of God sounds like a family. Some readers think that is why the Bible uses it.

words.d: a Bible name for heavenly ones who live near God

look.title: Two Names, One Group
look.text: Your teacher has a name. The class may call her Ms. Lee. Her kids call her Mom. It is the same person with two names. The Bible has two names for heavenly helpers: angels and sons of God.
look.prompt: What are the two names the Bible uses for heavenly helpers?

check.q: What is another Bible name for heavenly helpers?
check.why: The Bible calls heavenly ones angels. It also calls them sons of God.

check.q: Which book tells of the sons of God standing before God?
check.why: Job, chapter 1, tells of a day when the sons of God came before God.

check.q: What does the word son make you think of?
check.why: A son is part of a family. So sons of God sounds like a family.

lessons.title: Singing When the World Was New
lessons.mainIdea: Job 38:7 says heavenly ones sang for joy when the world was made.
reading: In the book of Job, God talks about the world. God says he set the earth in place. He laid it like the stone base of a house.
Then the story says something happy. When the world was made, the sons of God shouted for *joy*. The morning stars sang together. This is in Job 38:7.
So the Bible pictures a big party. The heavenly ones watched the world begin. They sang and cheered. It was a glad, happy day.

words.d: a big, happy feeling

look.title: A Song at the Start
look.text: When God made the world, the morning stars sang together. All the sons of God shouted for joy.
look.cite: Job 38:7, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: How did the sons of God feel when the world was made?

check.q: What did the sons of God do when the world was made?
check.why: Job 38:7 says the sons of God shouted for joy when the world was made.

check.q: What does joy mean?
check.why: Joy is a big, happy feeling, like singing and cheering.

check.q: Which verse tells about the singing?
check.why: Job 38:7 tells of the morning stars singing and the sons of God shouting for joy.

lessons.title: A Teacher Named Michael Heiser
lessons.mainIdea: Michael Heiser read the Bible's old languages and called the heavenly ones God's family.
reading: The Bible was first written in old languages. Most of it was in Hebrew. Some was in Greek. Michael Heiser was a teacher who read these old languages.
Heiser wrote books about the Bible's unseen world. He thought the heavenly ones were like God's *family* in heaven. They live with God in his home.
Other readers call angels God's servants or workers. Heiser knew they serve God too. But he often used the family picture. He saw it in names like sons of God.

words.d: the old language most of the Old Testament was first written in
people who belong together and share a home

look.title: Some of Heiser's Books
look.cite: Michael S. Heiser, books published by Lexham Press

check.q: What did Michael Heiser read?
check.why: Heiser was a teacher who read the Bible's old languages, like Hebrew and Greek.

check.q: What did Heiser call the heavenly ones?
check.why: Heiser thought the heavenly ones were like God's family in heaven.

check.q: What do some other readers call angels?
check.why: Some readers call angels God's servants or workers. Heiser often used the family picture.

lessons.title: Messengers With Good News
lessons.mainIdea: In the Bible, angels are messengers who bring news.
reading: The Hebrew word for angel means *messenger*. A messenger brings news. A mail carrier is a kind of messenger.
Luke, chapter 2, tells a story. Shepherds watched sheep at night. An angel came to them. The angel said, do not be afraid. I bring good news of great joy.
The angel told them a baby was born. His name was Jesus. Then many angels praised God. The shepherds went to see the baby.

words.d: someone who brings news from one person to another

look.title: Good News at Night
look.text: The angel said to the shepherds: Do not be afraid. I bring you good news. It is news of great joy for all people.
look.cite: Luke 2:10, retold in simple words from the World English Bible
look.prompt: What kind of news did the angel bring?

check.q: What does a messenger do?
check.why: A messenger brings news. The Hebrew word for angel means messenger.

check.q: Who heard the angel's news in Luke 2?
check.why: Luke 2 tells of shepherds watching sheep at night when an angel came.

check.q: What did the angel say first?
check.why: The angel told the shepherds not to be afraid. Then he gave good news.

review.q: How do we know the wind is there?
choices: We see what it does and feel it
review.why: The wind is unseen. We know it is there by what it does.

review.q: What does the Bible call God's home?
review.why: The Bible tells of heaven as God's home.

review.q: What are two Bible names for heavenly helpers?
review.why: The Bible calls heavenly helpers angels. It also calls them sons of God.

review.q: What does Job 38:7 say happened when the world was made?
review.why: Job 38:7 says the sons of God shouted for joy.

review.q: What did Michael Heiser call the heavenly ones?
review.why: Heiser, a teacher who read the Bible's old languages, called them God's family in heaven.

review.q: What does the Hebrew word for angel mean?
review.why: The Hebrew word for angel means messenger. Angels in the Bible bring news.

chapters.title: A Garden Home
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the Garden of Eden story tell about choices and care?

story.title: Planting Day
story.kicker: Theo and his mom plant seeds. Theo dreams of a garden where everyone gets along.
paragraphs: It is Saturday morning in the backyard. Theo kneels in the soft dirt. Mom hands him a small bag of bean seeds. "Two seeds in each hole," she says. Theo counts carefully.
Theo pats the dirt down. He pours water from his green can. A robin hops close. It pecks at a worm. A bee buzzes past the tomato plants. Theo does not chase them.
"Mom," Theo asks, "what if there was a garden where everyone got along? The birds and the bees and the people?" Mom smiles. "The Bible starts with a story like that," she says.
"It is about a garden called Eden," Mom says. "God made it. People lived there. It is a story about caring, and about choices." Theo wipes his hands. "Tell me," he says.
story.think: What would a garden where everyone gets along look like? Draw it or tell a friend.

lessons.title: In the Beginning
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 1 tells that God made the world, step by step.
reading: The first book of the Bible is called *Genesis*. Genesis means beginning. It starts with a story about how the world was made.
The story says God made light first. Then sky. Then land and plants. Then the sun, moon and stars. Then fish, birds and animals.
Last of all, the story says God made people. He looked at all he made. The story says it was very good. You can read this in Genesis, chapter 1.

words.d: the first book of the Bible; its name means beginning

look.title: The First Four Days
look.prompt: On which day does the story say plants were made?

check.q: What does the name Genesis mean?
check.why: Genesis means beginning. It is the first book of the Bible.

check.q: What does the story say God made first?
check.why: Genesis 1 says God made light first.

check.q: What did the story say God made last?
check.why: Genesis 1 says God made people last of all. Then he said it was very good.

lessons.title: A Garden Called Eden
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 2 tells of a garden home called Eden.
reading: Genesis, chapter 2, tells more. God planted a garden. It was in a place called *Eden*. God put the first man there.
The garden had many trees. They were nice to look at. They had good fruit to eat. A river flowed out of Eden to water it.
Later the story says God walked in the garden. It was the cool of the day. So Eden was a place where people and God could be together.

words.d: the garden home in the Bible's first story

look.title: A Picture of Eden
look.text: Picture a green garden. Tall trees hold red and yellow fruit. A clear river runs through the middle. Birds sing. The air is cool in the evening. It is calm and safe.
look.prompt: What things in this picture come from the Eden story?

check.q: What was the name of the garden?
check.why: Genesis 2 says God planted a garden in Eden.

check.q: What flowed out of Eden?
check.why: Genesis 2 says a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden.

check.q: When does the story say God walked in the garden?
choices: In the cool of the day
check.why: The story says God walked in the garden in the cool of the day.

lessons.title: Made to Care for the World
lessons.mainIdea: The story says people were made to take care of the garden.
reading: In Genesis 2, God put the man in the garden. He gave him a job. The job was to work the garden and keep it.
To keep a garden means to *care* for it. You water it. You pull weeds. You keep it safe. The man also gave names to the animals.
Then God made a woman, Eve. Now the man had a partner. Genesis 1 says God gave the care of the world to both of them.

words.d: to look after something and keep it safe

look.title: Caring Jobs
look.text: Look at the class fish tank. Mia feeds the fish. Jon wipes the glass. Sara checks the water. Each one has a job. Together they keep the fish healthy.
look.prompt: What jobs do you do to care for something at home or school?

check.q: What job did God give the man in Genesis 2?
choices: To work the garden and keep it
check.why: Genesis 2 says God put the man in the garden to work it and keep it.

check.q: What does it mean to care for a garden?
choices: To look after it and keep it safe
check.why: To care means to look after something, like watering and weeding.

check.q: What did the man give to the animals?
check.why: The story says the man gave names to the animals.

lessons.title: Where Heaven and Earth Met
lessons.mainIdea: Heiser saw Eden as God's home on earth, where both of God's families met.
reading: Remember Michael Heiser? He read the Bible's old languages. He thought hard about the Eden story.
Heiser saw Eden as God's home on earth. He thought God's heavenly family was there. God's earthly family, the people, was there too. In Eden, the two families met.
Other readers see Eden more simply. They see a lovely garden God made for people. Both readers agree it was a good place where God was near.

words.d: living on the earth, like people and animals
living in heaven with God

look.title: Two Ways to Read Eden
look.text: Reader one says: Eden was God's home on earth. His heavenly family and his earthly family met there. Reader two says: Eden was a lovely garden God made for people to live in.
look.prompt: Which reader is like Michael Heiser? What do both readers agree on?

check.q: How did Heiser see Eden?
check.why: Heiser saw Eden as God's home on earth, where God's two families met.

check.q: Who was God's earthly family in Heiser's picture?
check.why: Heiser called people God's earthly family. The heavenly ones were his heavenly family.

check.q: What do other readers see in Eden?
choices: A lovely garden God made for people
check.why: Other readers see Eden more simply, as a lovely garden God made for people.

lessons.title: The Shining One's Trick
lessons.mainIdea: In Genesis 3, a serpent tricked Eve into doubting God's words.
reading: God gave the people one rule. Do not eat from one special tree. They could eat from all the others. You can read this in Genesis 2.
Then a *serpent* came to Eve. It said the fruit would not hurt her. It tricked her. It made her doubt God's words. This is in Genesis 3.
Many readers see a snake here. Later Christian readers linked it with Satan. Heiser thought it was a shining one from God's heavenly family who chose wrong.

words.d: an old word for a snake; in Genesis 3, the one who tricked Eve
to fool someone into believing something that is not true

look.title: Three Readers, One Story
look.text: One reader says: the serpent was a snake. Another says: it was Satan. Heiser said: it was a shining heavenly one who chose to go against God. All three agree it tricked Eve.
look.prompt: What do all three readers agree the serpent did?

check.q: What did the serpent do to Eve?
check.why: Genesis 3 says the serpent tricked Eve and made her doubt God's words.

check.q: What did Heiser think the serpent was?
choices: A shining heavenly one who chose wrong
check.why: Heiser thought the serpent was a shining one from God's heavenly family who chose wrong.

check.q: What does serpent mean?
choices: An old word for a snake
check.why: Serpent is an old word for a snake. Genesis 3 uses it for the one who tricked Eve.

lessons.title: Choosing Not to Listen
lessons.mainIdea: Adam and Eve chose not to listen, and they had to leave the garden.
reading: Eve ate fruit from the special tree. She gave some to Adam. He ate it too. They chose not to listen to God's rule.
Then they felt bad inside. They hid from God among the trees. God called out to them. He asked what they had done.
Their *choice* changed things. The story says they had to leave the garden. Genesis 3 ends with them living outside Eden.

words.d: picking one thing to do instead of another

look.title: A Choice at Snack Time
look.text: Your teacher says: wait for everyone before you eat snack. You are very hungry. Your friend says: just take one now. You stop. You think. Now you must choose what to do.
look.prompt: What helps you stop and think before you make a choice?

check.q: What did Adam and Eve do after they ate the fruit?
check.why: Genesis 3 says they hid from God among the trees.

check.q: What is a choice?
choices: Picking one thing to do instead of another
check.why: A choice is picking one thing to do instead of another.

check.q: What happened because of their choice?
choices: They had to leave the garden
check.why: The story says they had to leave the garden after their choice.

lessons.title: God Still Cared
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 3:21 says God made clothes for Adam and Eve before they left.
reading: Adam and Eve had to leave Eden. But the story does not end with God walking away. God did something kind first.
God made clothes for them. He dressed them. This is in Genesis 3:21. The story shows that God still *cared* for them.
Choices matter. A wrong choice can change things. But the story shows care after a wrong choice. And each day, people can make new, good choices.

words.d: showed love by helping and looking after someone

look.title: Clothes From God
look.text: The LORD God made coats of skin for Adam and his wife. He put the clothes on them.
look.cite: Genesis 3:21, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What kind thing did God do for Adam and Eve?

check.q: What did God make for Adam and Eve?
check.why: Genesis 3:21 says God made clothes for Adam and Eve.

check.q: What does the clothes story show?
check.why: Making clothes for them shows God still cared, even after their wrong choice.

check.q: What can people do each day?
check.why: The lesson says choices matter, and each day people can make new, good choices.

review.q: What is the first book of the Bible?
review.why: Genesis is the first book of the Bible. It starts with how the world was made.

review.q: What job did God give people in the garden?
review.why: Genesis 2 says the man was put in the garden to work it and keep it.

review.q: How did Heiser see the Garden of Eden?
choices: As God's home on earth where his two families met
review.why: Heiser saw Eden as God's home on earth, where his heavenly and earthly families met.
Genesis 3 says the serpent tricked Eve.

review.q: What happened after Adam and Eve chose not to listen?
choices: They had to leave the garden
review.why: The story says they had to leave the garden.

review.q: What does Genesis 3:21 say God did?
choices: Made clothes for Adam and Eve
review.why: Genesis 3:21 says God made clothes for them. It shows he still cared.
